fact_sheet.business_description: The Company owns recurring entertainment franchises across consoles, personal computers and mobile phones [D01]. It generates revenue through premium games, subscriptions, in-game content and advertising [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Premium games, subscriptions, in-game content and advertising sold to users of consoles, PCs and mobile devices [D01]. Loyalty is driven by habitual engagement with long-standing franchises [D01].
economics: High operating margins (42% GAAP, 44% non-GAAP in Q2 2021) [D01]. Capital-intensive software production requires ongoing creative investment; intellectual property is not a self-maintaining royalty stream [D01].
Maintenance capex and owner-earnings inputs: not in pack.
earnings_record: Q2 2021 GAAP revenue $2.296 billion vs $1.932 billion year prior; diluted EPS $1.12 vs $0.75 [D01]. TTM operating cash flow of $2.57 billion [D01]. Cyclicality: reliance on creative investment and potential pandemic-period engagement levels [D05].
competitive_position: Portfolio includes large accumulated development libraries [D01]. Competitors include Electronic Arts, Take-Two and other mobile publishers [D06]. Moat evidence: habitual engagement and established franchises [D01].
management_and_capital_allocation: Management acknowledges serious workplace, compensation and employment allegations, creating a cloud over the company [D01].
Capital allocation record: not in pack.
price_and_valuation: P/E, P/B, earnings yield vs long bond: not in pack.
October 29, 2021 close: not in pack [D02, D04].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Serious employment, compensation and workplace allegations affecting management credibility and employee retention [D01, D05].
Predictability of franchise revenue versus fixed royalties [D05].
recent_events: August 3, 2021: results release acknowledging allegations and reporting Q2 financials [D01, D07].
berkshire_context: Berkshire cash at June 2021 was approximately $144.1 billion [D08]. Investment would be a passive public-equity holding; potential deputy-scale position [D08].
Tax basis/regulatory thresholds: not in pack.
missing_data: Full 5-10 year earnings/ROE record; precise maintenance capex; debt/liquidity details; share price as of 2021-10-31.

final.memo:
We have examined this business and found it to be unsuitable for Berkshire. While the company owns long-standing franchises that generate habitual engagement, the business model relies heavily on constant, capital-intensive creative reinvestment rather than the self-maintaining royalty streams we prefer [D01]. Intellectual property in this sector is not a static asset but one requiring ongoing, unpredictable cycles of development [D01].

Most troubling are the serious workplace, compensation, and employment allegations that have created a significant cloud over the management team [D01, D05]. We have a long-standing rule against investing in businesses where management credibility is in question or where our reputation could be compromised [D01, D05]. We insist on managers who act like owners and operate with unimpeachable integrity; the current governance situation falls far short of this standard [D01].

Furthermore, the pack does not provide the multi-year record of returns on capital necessary to judge the resilience of the business across cycles [D01]. Without clear data on maintenance capital expenditures or debt, we cannot determine intrinsic value or ensure a sufficient margin of safety [D01]. The market may be focusing on recent pandemic-period performance, but we must look to the long-term durability of the earnings stream, which remains unproven here [D01, D05].

We prefer to hold cash rather than deploy capital into situations characterized by structural instability and management uncertainty [D01, D08]. Our capital is better preserved for businesses with proven, durable moats and management teams in whom we have absolute confidence [D08]. Consequently, we have placed this opportunity in the 'too hard' pile.
